source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Under DOH AO 2011-0005, Informed Choice and Voluntarism (ICV) in family planning means the client:
options: Decides freely after full, accurate information
Follows the method the midwife recommends
Accepts a method to receive a cash incentive
Chooses only from methods in stock
questions.rationale: ICV ensures clients freely decide based on accurate, complete information on a broad range of modern methods, without inducement or coercion.
explanations: Clients must learn of all methods and be referred if unavailable.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 1 Informed Choice and Voluntarism (PDF p. 21)
questions.quote: ensuring that clients freely make their own decision based on accurate and complete information on a broad range of available modern FP methods

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A lying-in owner docks a midwife's pay for failing to reach 10 postpartum IUD insertions a month. Which ICV principle is violated?
questions.rationale: Providers must not implement or be subject to quotas or targets for numbers of acceptors of a method.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 1 Principles of ICV (PDF p. 23)
questions.quote: Service providers or referral agents shall not implement or be subject to quotas or other numerical targets

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A barangay health center refuses to immunize the babies of mothers who decline family planning. This violates the principle that:
options: No right or benefit is denied to non-acceptors
Only natural methods may be funded
Counseling must be done face to face
questions.rationale: Facilities shall not deny any right or benefit, including access to health care, because a client declines FP.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 1 Principles of ICV (PDF p. 23)
questions.quote: Mothers who did not accept any FP method are denied immunization services.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A woman in painful active labor is asked to sign consent for bilateral tubal ligation. What is wrong with this practice?
options: Consent under duress is not voluntary
questions.rationale: Informed consent for permanent methods must be voluntary and documented after counseling, not obtained while the client is in painful labor.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 1 Principles of ICV (PDF p. 24)
questions.quote: While Sally was in painful labor, she was asked to sign the consent for BTL.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A client wants BTL but no surgeon is available. What should the nurse do?
options: Refer her to a facility that offers BTL
Send her home without a method
Tell her BTL is not allowed
questions.rationale: Programs must give access to a broad range of methods directly or through referral.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 1 Principles of ICV (PDF p. 24)
questions.quote: the provider should be able to refer the client to a facility where the services are available

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: How does informed consent differ from informed choice in family planning?
options: It is the same as choice
questions.rationale: Informed consent is the client's written voluntary decision to accept a method (sterilization, IUD, implant) before the procedure, after counseling.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 1 Informed Consent (PDF p. 24)
questions.quote: Informed consent is a written voluntary decision of an FP client stating that he/she accepts the particular method

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Under the RPRH Act IRR as cited by DOH, a 17-year-old who already has a child asks for pills. What is required?
options: Written consent of a parent or guardian
No consent because she is a mother
questions.rationale: Minors, including those with a previous pregnancy, need written parental or guardian consent for FP services.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 1 RPRH Act provisions (PDF p. 25)
questions.quote: Any minor who has had a previous pregnancy or is already a parent still requires parental consent

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which consent is required before a married woman undergoes bilateral tubal ligation?
questions.rationale: Spousal consent is needed before permanent surgical contraceptive methods.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 1 RPRH Act provisions (PDF p. 25)
questions.quote: Spousal consent is needed prior to undergoing permanent surgical contraceptive methods.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: In the GATHER counseling approach, what does the 'H' stand for?
questions.rationale: GATHER: Greet, Ask, Tell, Help, Explain, Return visits.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 2 GATHER (PDF p. 33)
questions.quote: H – Help clients make informed choices.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: During the 'Tell' step of GATHER, the nurse should:
options: Describe choices, including using no method
Discuss only the method she prefers
Choose the method for the client
questions.rationale: Tell clients their choices, including no method, focusing on those of interest but briefly mentioning others.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 2 GATHER (PDF p. 33)
questions.quote: tell them what reproductive health choices they have, including FP methods or using no method at all

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which technique best confirms that a client understood how to use her chosen method?
options: Ask her to repeat the instructions
questions.rationale: Asking the client to repeat the instructions avoids misunderstandings, since many failures come from usage errors.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 2 Use of the chosen method (PDF p. 31)
questions.quote: A useful approach is to ask the client to repeat the instructions to avoid misunderstandings.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: In the ABCDE of safe sex, what does 'D' stand for?
questions.rationale: ABCDE: Abstinence, Being mutually faithful, Condom use, Do not share needles, Education and information.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 2 STI prevention (PDF p. 31)
questions.quote: Do not share needles

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A 16-year-old asks the nurse about contraception. Which approach is correct?
questions.rationale: Adolescents need confidential, age-appropriate counseling about all methods and abstinence; do not assume sexual activity. Family participation is encouraged.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 2 Counseling adolescents (PDF p. 35)
questions.quote: Providers must not assume that adolescents are sexually active simply because they are seeking FP services.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which statement must be explained before obtaining consent for sterilization?
options: She can change her mind any time before surgery
Temporary methods are no longer available
questions.rationale: Six elements include that temporary methods exist, it is surgery with risks, it is permanent, and the client can decide against it any time without losing benefits.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 2 Informed consent for permanent methods (PDF p. 35)
questions.quote: The client can decide against the procedure at any time before it takes place

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Who signs the FP consent form for a client who cannot give informed consent because of intellectual disability?
questions.rationale: If the client cannot give informed consent, the parent or legal guardian signs.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 2 Ensuring informed consent (PDF p. 34)
questions.quote: the parent or legal guardian must sign the consent form

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Under the WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria, Category 4 means:
options: Unacceptable health risk; do not use
questions.rationale: Category 1 no restriction; 2 advantages outweigh risks; 3 risks usually outweigh advantages; 4 unacceptable risk.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 3 WHO MEC categories (PDF p. 38)
questions.quote: A condition where the use of a certain method has an unacceptable health risk. Do not provide the method.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: In a barangay setting with limited clinical judgment, a client with an MEC Category 3 condition is:
questions.rationale: With limited clinical judgment, categories 1–2 mean use; categories 3–4 mean do not use.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 3 Simplified MEC (PDF p. 38)
questions.quote: a Category 3 classification indicates that a client is not medically eligible to use the method

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Before which method is a pelvic examination mandatory?
questions.rationale: Pelvic exam must be performed for IUD, surgical sterilization, or diaphragm.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 3 Physical examination (PDF p. 41)
questions.quote: It must be performed on all women requesting an IUD, surgical sterilization, or diaphragm insertion.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A woman wants pills but her blood pressure cannot be measured at the remote health station. According to WHO guidance in the manual:
options: Do not deny hormonal methods for this reason
questions.rationale: BP is ideally taken, but women should not be denied hormonal methods simply because BP cannot be measured where pregnancy risks are high.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 3 Applicability of tests (PDF p. 43)
questions.quote: women should not be denied the use of hormonal methods simply because their blood pressure cannot be measured

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which client can the nurse be reasonably sure is free of pregnancy without a test?
questions.rationale: A woman who gave birth within the last 4 weeks, started menses within 7 days, or aborted within 7 days is not pregnant.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 3 Ruling out pregnancy (PDF p. 44)
questions.quote: She gave birth within the last four weeks.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A client's answers cannot rule out pregnancy and no test is available. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: She should have a pregnancy test or wait for her next period, using condoms meanwhile.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 3 Ruling out pregnancy (PDF p. 45)
questions.quote: wait until her next menstrual period before starting a method. She should be provided with condoms

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which record documents a family planning client's assessment and follow-up visits?
questions.rationale: FP Form 1 records history, PE, lab results, and every follow-up visit.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 3 Recording assessment (PDF p. 48)
questions.quote: The basic record used in assessing a client’s condition is the Family Planning Service Record or FP Form 1

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: How often should a woman perform breast self-examination once she has mastered it?
questions.rationale: Self-exam weekly until mastered, then monthly, preferably one week after menstruation.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 3 Physical examination (PDF p. 41)
questions.quote: preferably one week after every menstruation
